sections.h2: What should a Warwick homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
Selling in Warwick comes with one cost most New York sellers never meet: a town transfer tax paid by the buyer, which shapes how offers are priced. Beyond that, the town is large, rural in parts and split among several school districts, so where your house sits matters as much as its condition. Know your hamlet, your district and your assessment before you talk numbers.

The Town of Warwick fills the southwestern tip of Orange County, along the New Jersey line. It spans about 105 square miles, making it one of the largest towns in the state, and counted 32,027 residents in 2020. Inside it are three incorporated villages (Warwick, Florida and Greenwood Lake) and a string of hamlets that include Amity, Bellvale, Edenville, Pine Island, Sterling Forest and Wisner.

Several of the hamlets have their own character. Pine Island is the commercial center of the black dirt farmland, Edenville lies in the western part of town off County Route 1, and Sterling Forest and Greenwood Lake sit along the New Jersey line. Warwick also hosts the annual Applefest each October, which Wikipedia says draws as many as 35,000 visitors.

sections.h2: What do homes and land look like across the Town of Warwick?
sections.html:
Warwick mixes village streets, lake communities and farmland. Land around Pine Island and Hoopstick sits in the Black Dirt region, known for good agricultural soil, while Greenwood Lake straddles the New York and New Jersey border. The Appalachian Trail passes through town, and Warwick is an Appalachian Trail Community.

The area was settled in the early 1700s, when patent holder Benjamin Aske named his land Warwick and began selling parcels in 1719. During the Revolution the Hudson River Chain was forged at Sterling Iron Works here. More recently the former Mid-Orange Correctional Facility, which closed in 2011, was handed to the town in 2014. Part of its grounds became Wickham Woodlands Park, and the rest became the Warwick Valley Office and Technology Corporate Park.

  • Warwick village: centered where NY 94 meets NY 17A.
  • Florida and Greenwood Lake villages: also on NY 17A.
  • Pine Island and the Black Dirt hamlets: farmland and larger lots.
  • Amity, Edenville and New Milford: near the New Jersey line.

sections.h2: Which school district and commute applies to my Warwick address?
sections.html:
Most of the town lies in the Warwick Valley Central School District, but other parts belong to the Florida Union Free School District, the Greenwood Lake Union Free School District and the Tuxedo Union Free School District. A buyer's first question is often which school their children will attend, so confirm your district before you list rather than guessing from the mailing address.

Two state highways, NY 17A and NY 94, carry most traffic, and Warwick Municipal Airport serves the town. New Jersey Transit buses 196 and 197 run to Manhattan, and a Warwick inter-municipal bus also serves the town. Winter matters for a house here: NOAA data cited for the town shows about 38.9 inches of snow and 44.7 inches of precipitation in a typical year, so roof age and drainage often come up in inspections.

sections.h2: How does Warwick's community preservation transfer tax work?
sections.html:
Warwick charges a three-quarters of one percent transfer tax on property sales, and the buyer pays it. Voters approved it by referendum in November 2006, and it has applied to conveyances since April 1, 2007, including those inside the villages. The money goes into a fund for open space, farmland, recreation, water resources and historic structures.

The first $100,000 of the price of improved property is exempt from the tax, and the first $50,000 for unimproved land. On a $450,000 house, the taxable amount is $350,000, so the buyer's town tax would come to $2,625. The town's own transfer tax form goes to the county clerk together with the standard state form, and the deed is not recorded until both are in. Orange County's deed page lists a $5 fee for the Community Preservation Fund form and sends Warwick residents to the town for it.

Because the buyer carries this cost, ask any buyer whether the offer already accounts for it.

sections.h2: How are Warwick assessments and property taxes set?
sections.html:
The Town Assessor's office in Town Hall, 132 Kings Highway, sets assessments, and 2026 assessments in Warwick are at a uniform level of 7.65 percent of full value as of July 2025. That means a house worth $400,000 on the market would carry an assessment of roughly $30,600, so do not read a low assessed value as a low market value. Exemption applications are due March 1 each year, and the office begins taking the next year's applications in July.

An informal review request can be made before the town files its tentative roll on May 1, and the town suggests asking by March 15. Formal complaints go to the Board of Assessment Review on the fourth Tuesday of May. For 2026 that was May 26, so that date has passed and the next chance falls in May 2027.

Real property tax is collected by the Receiver of Taxes from January through March, and school tax from September through October. Unpaid taxes go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance at 255 Main Street in Goshen. Ask for a current bill and a payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: What permits and recording costs apply to a Warwick sale?
sections.html:
The Building Department enforces the state and town building codes and issues certificates of occupancy, which the town says are required for all building in Warwick. Its office is in Town Hall and is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:00. A five-member Zoning Board of Appeals hears requests for relief from the zoning laws. If your house has an open permit or a missing certificate of occupancy, resolve or disclose it before accepting an offer.

Deeds are recorded with the Orange County Clerk. The clerk's current fee list for a deed shows the amounts below, and payment must be cash or check, with no credit cards and no personal checks over $250.

Orange County Clerk deed recording charges
ChargeAmount
Flat recording fee$45
Each page$5
TP-584 transfer tax form$5
NYS deed fraud letter$10
RP-5217, single family or agricultural$125
RP-5217, commercial or vacant land$250
Community Preservation Fund form$5

The seller's state deed tax is two dollars per five hundred dollars of price, paid on top of these charges, while the Warwick tax above falls on the buyer.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a good fit for a Warwick house?
sections.html:
A cash offer fits when speed or condition outweighs getting the top price. Houses that struggle with a bank appraisal, such as ones with deferred repairs or an estate that has not settled, are the usual candidates. A cash buyer also works without a lender's timetable.

  • Compare the net you would receive after the transfer tax, payoff and any tax proration.
  • Ask whether the buyer will close at the Orange County Clerk or through a title company, and who pays for recording.
  • Keep the Warwick transfer tax form in the checklist so the deed is not rejected.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay Warwick's transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer pays it. Warwick's community preservation tax is three-quarters of one percent of the price, with the first $100,000 of an improved property exempt. The seller still owes the state deed tax of two dollars per five hundred dollars.

faqs.q: Who sets property assessments in the Town of Warwick?
faqs.a: The Town Assessor's office, in Warwick Town Hall at 132 Kings Highway. Its 2026 uniform level of assessment is 7.65 percent of full value, so assessed values sit far below market value. Exemption applications are due each March 1.

faqs.q: When were Warwick's 2026 assessment appeals heard?
faqs.a: On Tuesday, May 26, 2026, and that date has passed. The Board of Assessment Review meets on the fourth Tuesday of May, so the next hearing falls in May 2027. An informal review can be requested earlier, ideally by March 15.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed on a Warwick sale?
faqs.a: The Orange County Clerk. The deed page lists a $45 flat fee, $5 per page, $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 on a single family house, payable by cash or check. Personal checks over $250 are not accepted.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Warwick house?
faqs.a: Most of the town is in the Warwick Valley Central School District. Other parts fall in the Florida, Greenwood Lake or Tuxedo Union Free School Districts, so check the district for your exact parcel before you list.
